title: MapleStory Classic Hunter Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 30-70
intro: Hunters are the faster bow specialist built around crowd control. Arrow Bomb clears groups of mobs and stuns them in place, Amazon's Judgement slows anything that survives a critical hit, and Bow Booster keeps those arrows flying.

blocks.p: This guide is based off of a realistic lv 70 Hunter build by Grummash.
**Pros**

ul: #2 AoE damage at level 70, best long range AoE damage dealer.
Arrow Bomb hits up to four mobs and can stun for 3 seconds.
Shoots faster than Crossbowman. Pew pew.
Almost never has any Accuracy problems.
Soul Arrow lets you shoot without using up arrows.

blocks.p: **Cons**

ul: Inside 65 px your bow whacks a mob. It is a weak melee swing.
Arrow Bomb costs 28 MP at max and burns through Lemons on dense maps.
Final Attack is chance-based and can interfere with your skill rotations.
Probably the squishiest class in MapleStory Classic.
No movement skill in second job. You walk and jump to every platform.

blocks.p: This guide continues from the Bowman level 1 to 30 guide. Its no-reset endpoint is Arrow Blow 20, Critical Shot 15, The Eye of Amazon 15, Focus 10, and Power Knockback 1.

Grummash's saved level 70 build uses Double Shot 20, Arrow Blow 1, and Focus 9. If you want that exact endpoint, move 19 SP from Arrow Blow and 1 from Focus into Double Shot. The live Cash Shop price for this reset is unconfirmed.
Keep Henesys citizenship from the first-job guide. Its rewards cover arrows, Accuracy consumables, DEX options, and weapon scrolls for both Bowman branches.

A training map only works when your attacks connect. But who are we kidding? You're a Hunter. You have so much Accuracy that unless you're fighting mobs well above your level, you don't have Accuracy issues.

blocks.h2: Levels 30-70: Hunter skill build and leveling

ol: Start the second-job advancement with Athena Pierce in Henesys.
Take Athena's letter to the Bowman Job Instructor at The Road to the Dungeon.
Kill the test mobs until you have 30 Dark Marbles, then exchange them for The Proof of a Hero.
Return to Athena Pierce and choose Hunter.

blocks.p: Second-job SP cannot be spent on first-job skills, so finish the first-job plan by level 30. Character Builder flags any build that breaks it.

blocks.note: **Why Mastery and Booster come first:** At level 35, this sample build improved from about 3,240 to 4,420 Advisor EXP/min. At level 40, it improved from 8,370 to 9,400 EXP/min. Stronger low rolls and faster attacks beat rushing Arrow Bomb for these checkpoints.

blocks.h3: Possible changes to the default order

blocks.p: Max Arrow Bomb immediately when grouped mobs already die cleanly. You give up early Mastery, Booster, and Soul Arrow.
After maxing Arrow Bomb, you can max Amazon's Judgement before Final Attack. The slow can help keep mobs from reaching you. You give up the earlier chance of a follow-up attack though.
Final Attack has a 50% proc at max. Disable it when Training Advisor already shows a guaranteed one-shot and the follow-up would waste time.
This continues from 30 base STR and 132 base DEX. Golden Hinkel requires 70 STR, so the simple one-STR-per-level plan lands exactly on the requirement.

blocks.p: Bows use both hands, so Hunters cannot equip a shield. Carry enough arrows until Soul Arrow has comfortable uptime. While Soul Arrow is active, attacks do not consume arrows.

blocks.h3: Where to get Vaulter 2000 and Olympus

blocks.p: Start Woodcrafting by level 25 if you want the Olympus at 50. No shop sells the Vaulter 2000, the Olympus, or the Asianic Bow. The Vaulter 2000 is a Woodcrafting 8 recipe. The Olympus is a Woodcrafting 10 recipe. Your character level caps your crafting level at five times the craft level, so Woodcrafting 8 opens at level 40 and Woodcrafting 10 at level 50. Same levels as the bows.
Vicious, the carpenter of Henesys, teaches Woodcrafting. His starter quest, Vicious in Need of an Apprentice, opens at level 10 and asks you to defeat 30 Stumps and collect 20 Tree Branches.

blocks.p: Iron Arrows for Bows are a Woodcrafting 7 recipe: 500 arrows from 1 Processed Wood, 1 Iron Ingot, and 1 Stiff Feather. Adamantium Arrows for Bows are Woodcrafting 10: 1 Processed Wood, 1 Adamantium Ingot, and 12 Stiff Feather. No shop sells either, so this is your best place to get them aside from the Free Market.

blocks.h2: W.ATK or Critical Rate on gloves?

blocks.p: These numbers use Grummash's realistic level 70 Hunter build and five successful Lesser glove scrolls. Both options use the same five slots.

**+5 W.ATK**
98 to 103 total W.ATK
About 5.1% more expected damage.

**+5% Critical Rate**
31% to 36% Critical Rate
About 1.82% more expected damage.

blocks.note: **Pick Attack.** The five-scroll Attack setup deals about 3.22% more expected damage than the Critical Rate setup on this build.

blocks.p: Critical Shot raises this build to 41% Critical Damage, so Critical Rate is worth more for Hunter than it is for a Warrior. W.ATK still wins at level 70.

**The ratio is the same at every grade.** Lesser gives +1 W.ATK or +1% Critical Rate (+2 M.ATK), Intermediate +2/+2% (+4 M.ATK), Greater +3/+3% (+6 M.ATK), and Chaos +4/+4% (+8 M.ATK). Matching grades have the same success and destruction rates.

**W.ATK also helps guaranteed kills.** It raises every physical hit, including your weakest normal roll and every critical hit. Critical Rate changes how often a critical occurs, so it cannot improve the weakest non-critical roll.

blocks.p: **Before you settle in:** The Arrow Bomb picks assume each shot reaches its full four-mob cap. Test a few groups of mobs before settling in. If mobs keep closing to whack range, choose platforms with more shooting room. Count Arrow Bomb casts on the whole group; the single-target damage number does not describe every mob in it.
Arrow Bomb fires at one mob and the linked explosion hits up to four mobs total, including the first target. Max level deals 140% damage with a 60% chance to stun for 3 seconds.
**Four targets need to stay grouped.** Arrow Bomb's four-target damage assumes the explosion reaches all four mobs. Spread-out mobs reduce the damage you get per cast.
There are user reports of testers outside North America experiencing delayed explosions or mobs not getting hit as expected. High ping is a suspected cause, but remains unconfirmed.
**Warning: Arrow Bomb with high ping may be very annoying to use.**
**At level 70, the benchmark deals about 6,217 expected total damage when four targets are available.**

Max Final Attack has a 50% chance to fire three 90% arrows after your skill. The arrows split like Holy Arrow: all three hit a lone mob, two and one split across two mobs, and three mobs take one each. It is a toggle.

Each FA proc has its own attack animation, and you can't attack again until it ends: about 0.6 seconds with Booster. Hunter's Final Attack: Bow is always a damage boost if you're using Double Shot. It may be a damage boost when using Arrow Bomb, depending on the number of targets.
The shot goes the way you face when it fires. Hold the opposite direction to send it at a mob behind you. With no mob in front, it doesn't fire.

table: Max Final Attack on vs off

blocks.p: Final Attack costs no MP, so it also saves potions: about 56 % more damage per MP against one mob and 24 % against four. Each proc uses up 3 arrows unless Soul Arrow is active.
Every critical hit applies the slow at max level. The target loses 35 Speed for 5 seconds. Bow Mastery also adds 20 Evasion. Hunters get the defensive bonus of the two Bowman branches.

blocks.note: **Level 70 damage check:** At level 70, max Double Shot deals about 2,664 expected damage to one neutral target per cast. Max Arrow Bomb reaches about 6,217 expected total damage with four targets. Booster raises the modeled attack rate from 74 to 83 casts per minute.

blocks.h2: Find Your Build's Best Training Map with Training Advisor

blocks.p: **Danger measures how hard a mob hits you for: under 10% of your HP is Safe, 10-24% is Caution, 25-49% is Danger, and 50%+ is Lethal.**
Arrow Bomb changes the answer as its damage, Final Attack setting, and four-target uptime change. Check the saved character instead of copying one level-70 map.

ol: Load your Hunter in Character Builder with the bow, arrows, scrolls, skills, and buffs you actually use.
Select Double Shot for single targets or Arrow Bomb for grouped mobs, then set reliability to 100%.
Leave Factor Danger into recommendations enabled. It still matters for a ranged class, though melee builds receive the larger penalty.
Look for one- or two-attack kills, then check the map keeps mobs beyond 65 px.
Use Final Attack's real on or off setting. A proc cannot make the main hit a guaranteed kill.

Check the nearest potion and arrow shops. A nearest-town scroll gets you back to town quickly. Count the walk back to the map before picking a distant grind spot. Arrow restocks matter less once Soul Arrow has comfortable uptime.

ol: **Maxing Final Attack before Arrow Bomb.** Arrow Bomb gives reliable mobbing damage and control every cast. Final Attack only procs half the time at max.
**Bad positioning.** Leave space between yourself and the mob. Your bow whacks at close range by design, and you'll likely have to spend MP using Power Knockback to push mobs away.
**Running out of arrows before Soul Arrow has comfortable uptime.** Carry enough stacks to finish the training session.
**Picking maps by mob level.** Lower-level mobs you always clear in one cast can beat a higher-level target that needs three.
